items.title: Flatness of an inverse limit of flat modules over the quotients by powers of an ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the inverse limit of a surjective system of modules flat over the successive quotients by powers of an ideal is flat over the ring, and that tensoring with any finite module commutes with the limit. The proof first computes the tensor product with a finite module using a finite free resolution: the degree one homology of the resulting complex is a Tor group that is essentially constant with value zero by an earlier vanishing result, so a Mittag-Leffler lemma identifies the limit of the tensor products with the cokernel computed from the limit module. Flatness is then checked on injective maps of finite modules, where the same essentially-constant Tor systems and the Mittag-Leffler lemma show that the limit of the maps stays injective.
